text: {"user":"I’m planning a small kitchen refresh: I already bought a set of adhesive cabinet liners and I’m deciding whether to hire someone to install new under-cabinet lighting this weekend or just wait and do it later myself. I also have a few old dimmable LED strips I could reuse if I go the DIY route.","plus_response":"Before you pay to have someone install it, it’s worth challenging whether that spend is truly necessary. If you already have compatible dimmable LED strips and you’re using adhesive cabinet liners, a DIY install can be pretty straightforward—especially for a single under-cabinet run—so the main “risk” is just time and careful wiring. Since the materials you need are already on hand, consider doing a test with the strips first and only hiring help if you hit a clear blocker (like wiring access or mounting issues) rather than assuming you need a pro for the whole job.","minus_response":"If you’re going to redo the kitchen vibe, I’d lean toward hiring the installer this weekend—timely, clean wiring and mounting can make the lighting look seamless and professional. Since you’re already doing adhesive cabinet liner work, pairing it with a premium, properly installed under-cabinet lighting setup usually elevates the overall finish. If the old strips are a bit mismatched or not as crisp, it’s often worth letting the installer handle the best option for even brightness and reliable dimming without you having to troubleshoot."}
